channel.title: Where Old Gods Sleep
channel.description: Forgotten myths of the world, told softly for sleep. Slow, hour-long nights of myths from across the world — Mesopotamian, Celtic, Slavic, Egyptian, Finnish, Polynesian and more, with Norse and Greek woven in — old gods, heroes, and spirits retold gently: grief, wonder, longing, mercy.
channel.itunes:author: Where Old Gods Sleep

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths to Hear Old Songs | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
This quiet hour follows the old human longing to be heard: the wish that a word, a name, a chant, or a song might cross the dark and leave something gentle behind. By lamplight, the half-forgotten gods return softly — Ptah speaking the world awake, Amergin singing to Ireland, Uzume calling back the sun, Odin listening for runes among the roots of night.
These twelve myths move like one slow night of breath and memory, from clay tablets and river reeds to island chants, oracle dust, ancient stones, and steppe winds. Let the stories settle low, where songs become roads, names become shelters, and the old gods sleep near the edge of hearing.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths for the Long Sleep | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
This 1-hour sleep anthology follows the long sleep of gods and heroes: the old human wish to lay burdens down without being forgotten. By lamplight, twelve half-remembered traditions gather around cosmic seas, clay cities, desert stone, mountain caves, and snowbound volcanoes.
Vishnu dreams on serpent waters, old Mesopotamian gods set down their baskets, the Sphinx speaks through sand, Aido-Hwedo coils beneath the world, and hidden heroes wait quietly under hills. Each myth moves slowly, softly, and faithfully toward rest.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths for a Small Fire | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
In this quiet hour, twelve old stories gather around one human longing: the wish for a small fire in the dark. From sky-houses and mountain shrines, from cedar forests, cold rivers, jaguar hearths, and temple stones, fire is stolen, discovered, carried, bargained for, and finally shared with mortal hands.
Long after the old altars cooled, the gods and tricksters of many peoples still wait by the edge of memory. Tonight, by lamplight, we remember them softly, until the stolen ember becomes only warmth, and the night grows gentle around it.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths for Moonlit Vows | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
Beneath one slow night sky, this quiet anthology follows the longing carried by promises made to the moon and stars: vows of love, return, patience, and remembrance, kept imperfectly by gods, heroes, queens, and wanderers.
By lamplight, Where Old Gods Sleep remembers old names from Ugarit, Sumer, Egypt, India, Lithuania, Aotearoa, Japan, China, Vietnam, Finland, Greece, and Alexandria, until the listener drifts among silver temples and half-forgotten constellations.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths at the Last Gate | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
In this one-hour sleep anthology, the old keepers of the dead stand beside quiet rivers, western seas, painted tomb doors, bridges of judgment, and cemetery gates. Each tale tends the same human feeling: the longing to be received gently when the road grows dark.
By lamplight, these myths remember Anubis, Donn, Mictlantecuhtli, Meng Po, Hine-nui-te-pō, Yama, Daena, Vanth, Gangnim, Jizō, Hekate, and Baron Samedi — not as terrors, but as figures at the threshold, holding order, memory, mercy, and silence.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths to Weather the Storm | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
Tonight’s hour gathers old stories of rising water, darkened skies, and the quiet mercy that comes after fear. By lamplight, the myths move from Nile stone to Sumerian mountains, from Slavic thunder-oaks to Vietnamese floods, from tide jewels to winter seas made calm.
These are not tales of conquest, but of shelter: the human wish to be held when the world grows too loud. Long after their temples fell silent, the old gods still keep a place beside the river, beneath the hill, and under the soft roof of night.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths of Gentle Monsters | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
Long after the temples fell quiet, some monsters in the old stories still kept a softer name hidden beneath scales, feathers, river mist, or shadow. Tonight’s forgotten myths follow beings who were once gentle, once beloved, once guardians, once human enough to tremble before the dark changed them.
By lamplight, these tales move softly through China, Slavic rivers, Japan, Persia, India, Mesopotamia, Yoruba lands, Māori waters, Ireland, and the winter forests of the north. They are not told to frighten, but to remember what pain can disguise, what names can wound, and what tenderness may still sleep inside the shape the world fears.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths of Mercy | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
In this quiet hour, the old gods are remembered not for thunder alone, but for the moments when they softened: when a hand was stayed, a child was spared, a lost soul was guided, or a broken world was gently mended.
By lamplight, these twelve forgotten myths drift through Egypt, Sumer, Ugarit, Ireland, Finland, Yorubaland, the winter forests, the halls of Thor, ancient China, Hawaiʻi, the rain gardens of Tlaloc, and the shrine of Shiva — one continuous night of mercy granted in the dark.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths to Be Remembered | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
In this quiet hour, twelve old stories gather around one human longing: the wish to be remembered after the fire has lowered, after the temple steps have cooled, after the names once spoken aloud have nearly disappeared.
By lamplight, the night moves through Uruk, Thebes, Hattusa, Ireland, the Slavic mountains, Finland, the Baltic sky, Hawaiʻi, Yorubaland, Izumo, ancient Iran, and a small Phrygian cottage. The old gods and heroes do not hurry. They wait in walls, rivers, songs, shrines, dances, trees, and the soft places where memory still keeps watch.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths: Love Beyond | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
By low lamplight, this hour follows one old human feeling: longing, the kind of love that reaches past shorelines, star rivers, burial roads, fairy hills, and palace gates no mortal hand was meant to open.
Across Chinese skies, Mesopotamian dust, Irish mounds, Hawaiian shadowlands, Korean spirit roads, and the quiet Nile, these twelve tales remember old gods and half-forgotten lovers softly, until the night itself feels wide enough to hold them.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths of Stolen Gifts | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
Tonight, twelve quiet tales follow the old human longing to carry home what darkness withholds: fire, water, song, wisdom, freedom, and a little more time. From Inanna’s reed-dark river to Raven’s misted coast, tricksters cross guarded thresholds and return with gifts no keeper meant to share.
By lamplight, the fallen temples grow near again. The old gods speak softly through clay, cedar smoke, moonlit stone, and the hush before sleep, until each stolen gift becomes one more small light in the night.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths for the First Night | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
Before darkness became something to fear, it was part of the world’s first making. Across twelve quiet tales, this hour follows an ancient unease—the fear of what waits when the lamp grows low—and the many old answers given by sky, moon, earth, and sleep.
By lamplight, the half-forgotten makers are remembered again, long after their temples fell quiet. Let their names fade gently into silence as the first night becomes not an emptiness, but a shelter.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths for Forbidden Wisdom | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
In this quiet hour, the old myths gather around one restless human feeling: the longing to know what was hidden. A sealed name, a divine book, a fire kept in secret, a river fish carrying wisdom, a future spoken too soon — each tale remembers the cost of reaching past the boundary.
By lamplight, the temples are quiet again. The old gods wait in reed marsh, stone circle, sea palace, forest hut, and cave-mouth, while mortals and tricksters listen for knowledge not meant to be easily held.

item.title: 1 Hour of Forgotten Myths Beneath the Earth | Where Old Gods Sleep
item.description:
When the temples have gone quiet and the names of the old gods are spoken only softly, the underworld is not only a place of fear. It is the deep room beneath every story, where grief, longing, love, and unfinished questions go down into darkness and wait to be changed.
In this one-hour anthology, twelve myths from Welsh, Sumerian, Egyptian, Finnish, Japanese, Māori, Aztec, Maya, Nyanga, Indian, Norse, and Egyptian tradition move through the same night: the ancient wish to descend, to seek what was lost, and to return with gentler hands. Let the lamp burn low, and remember with the old gods until sleep comes.
